Segmentation: Feature Opportunity: ShiFt Happens for our Readership Growth Challenge
Feedback:
Dear [name],

My name is Yvonne [name], and I'm reaching out on behalf of the Oprah's
Book Club Official community on Goodreads, a vibrant public group of more
than 87,000 passionate readers who love discovering books that make a
genuine difference in their lives.

What Stood Out to Me

I recently came across ShiFt Happens: Stop Surviving. Start Owning. , and I
have to say, I was genuinely moved. This isn't another polished self-help
book filled with empty promises. It's raw, unfiltered, and built from real
experience—the kind of book that comes from hitting rock bottom and
deciding to rise anyway
<https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/description#1>
.

What struck me most is how honest the book seems to be about what
transformation actually costs. The author describes writing from rock
bottom, from trauma, from the grit of raising kids alone, going back to
school after 22 years, surviving toxic workplaces, rebuilding after
divorce, and learning to be unapologetically authentic
<https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/description#1>.
It's the kind of book that doesn't pretend healing is pretty. It
acknowledges the messy middle where you finally decide to stop shrinking
and start showing up for yourself
<https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/creator>
.

The SHIFT Framework—See It Clearly, Heal the Hurt, Integrate Your Identity,
Face the Fear, Take Aligned Action—sounds like a practical roadmap rather
than just inspiration
<https://www.iheart.com/podcast/269-own-the-shift-127074112/#1>. What makes
this approach distinctive is that healing and vision aren't treated as
separate steps. They're one movement, one practice you learn to live in
<https://www.audible.co.uk/podcast/Own-The-ShiFt/B0CM6RJSXR?ref_pageloadid=4J4x2jUrtf1ykaBc&plink=X1bu6iUfHCcNJ0GW&pageLoadId=VLC6KTDX0hISt7pf&creativeId=2b[number]fc-989c-4535caab7c59&ref=a_podcast_C_c1_podcast-show-details#1>.
The author's voice, described as "part science, part story, and part soul"
with "a side of sass," suggests this is a book that meets you where you are
and doesn't let you stay comfortable
<https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/description#1>
.

What Makes This Book Stand Out

   -

   Authenticity That Connects – This book didn't come from theory. It came
   from lived experience: trauma, healing, rebuilding, and learning to be
   unapologetically authentic
   <https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/description#1>.
   Readers connect with that kind of honesty. The author describes being just
   like so many of us—someone who spent years trying to outrun her past, prove
   her worth, and hold everything together while quietly falling apart
   <https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/creator>
   .
   -

   Practical Framework for Change – The SHIFT Framework provides a clear,
   actionable structure: See It Clearly, Heal the Hurt, Integrate Your
   Identity, Face the Fear, Take Aligned Action
   <https://www.iheart.com/podcast/269-own-the-shift-127074112/#1>
   <https://www.audible.co.uk/podcast/Own-The-ShiFt/B0CM6RJSXR?ref_pageloadid=4J4x2jUrtf1ykaBc&plink=X1bu6iUfHCcNJ0GW&pageLoadId=VLC6KTDX0hISt7pf&creativeId=2b[number]fc-989c-4535caab7c59&ref=a_podcast_C_c1_podcast-show-details#1>.
   It doesn't just tell you to change; it shows you how. The book includes
   reflection questions, journal prompts, and tools that make transformation
   something you can actually practice
   <https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/description#1>
   .
   -

   A Movement, Not Just a Book – This book is the foundation of a larger
   movement that includes the "Own The Shift" podcast and a growing community
   of people who are done living on autopilot
   <https://www.iheart.com/podcast/269-own-the-shift-127074112/#1>. It's
   for the resilient underdog who's done waiting for "later"
   <https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/description#1>
   .
   -

   Written for the People Who Need It Most – The author describes writing
   this book for the woman sitting in her car trying not to cry before walking
   into work, the dad doing everything to hold it together, the dreamer told
   it's "too late," the survivor who made it through hell but still feels
   unseen
   <https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/shifthappens/shift-happens-rewired-resilience-built-to-rise-0/description#1>.
   That kind of purpose makes this book feel urgent and necessary.

An Invitation to Our 6-Month Reading Challenge

We're currently curating our 6-month Readership Growth Challenge, a program
designed to connect passionate readers with exceptional books that spark
meaningful conversation. We're selecting only 21 authors total, and I

This is a wonderful opportunity to introduce your work to a large, engaged
audience that genuinely appreciates practical, authentic guidance for
personal transformation. It's about creating a space for readers to truly
engage with your work and for you to connect with an audience that values
exceptional, life-changing nonfiction.

Next Steps

We're finalizing the author lineup and would be delighted to include you.
The next step is to send you our community overview with full details about
the schedule, engagement structure, and what the feature looks like. Please

Thank you for writing a book that shows us the real kind of shift—the one

You are receiving this communication because you use Identity and Access

To support our customers' integration timelines and ensure seamless  
security, we have updated the scope of our upcoming release to uphold a  
strict separation of duties. Administrative functions will remain isolated  
from sensitive cryptographic key usage, and predefined viewer roles will  
continue to be restricted from execution capabilities and data access.

Please refer to the communication dated January 29, 2026 titled '[Action  
Advised] Review IAM new permissions for multiple Google Cloud services' and  
our subsequent March update titled '[Product Update] IAM Roles enhancements  
deferred until Sep 30, 2026' to learn more about the background of these  
modifications.

The details below outline the refined scope of these changes and describe  
recommended steps to review your IAM policies.

What you need to know

Key changes regarding the updated rollout:

The effective date for the change remains September 30, 2026, with adjusted  
scope. Please review the updated changes and engage with us on any  
questions or concerns during this period.

The following updates apply to the IAM predefined role release:


Predefined Viewer roles (such as Spanner Viewer, Bigtable Viewer, and  
Dataplex Viewer) remain restricted from access to underlying business data,  
execution capabilities, or source code. They will continue to grant  
read-only access to metadata.
Predefined Admin roles (such as Storage Admin and KMS Admin) remain  
isolated from long-lived credentials (HMAC) or cryptographic key usage  
permissions, ensuring security administration remains separated from  
resource usage.
Standardized Baselines for Administrative, Editor and metadata-viewing will  
be established across 85 predefined roles to simplify permission management.

What this means for your environment

The scheduled role adjustments help ensure that the upcoming rollout more  
seamlessly integrates with the existing security guardrails setup for your  
environment, by keeping Viewer roles restricted to metadata only, and  
keeping Admin functions separate from data access.

recommended actions:


Review permissions: Review the refined permissions granted to your  
principals across your policies where these roles are applied. Verify that  
the updated permissions align with your organization's security  
requirements.
Configure custom roles or deny policies: If you do not want to grant  
specific permissions to certain users, groups, or service accounts,  
implement one of the following alternatives:

Create a custom role with only the specific permissions you require. Refer  
to the guide on how to define a custom role.
Apply an IAM Deny policy to restrict specific permissions. Refer to the  
guide on how to use IAM Deny policies.


Note: If the updated role permissions are acceptable, you do not need to  
take any action.

predefined role changes. Complete all policy reviews and role  
configurations prior to this date.

Segmentation: Exploring the Power of Literature, Reflection, and Growth — A Note from 365 [name] Ministry
Feedback:
Hi SuperSummary Team,

I recently came across your *Study Guide: Esperanza Rising*, and I was
really drawn to the thoughtful way SuperSummary helps readers go beyond
simply finishing a book and instead pause to explore its themes,
characters, struggles, and deeper meaning.

What stood out to me was your focus on creating conversations around
literature. The way your guides encourage readers, educators, and book
clubs to think critically, ask meaningful questions, and connect more
deeply with what they’re reading feels especially valuable.

That resonates with the heart of 365 [name]. Our mission is to
capture and share stories and resources that uplift women through
Christ-centered encouragement. We believe stories can do more than
entertain—they can open conversations, help us reflect on our own
experiences, and give us new perspectives on growth, resilience, purpose,
and faith.

I feel that’s where our work naturally intersects. SuperSummary creates
tools that help readers engage thoughtfully with stories, while 365
[name] seeks to create meaningful conversations around stories and
resources that encourage women in their own journeys. There is something
powerful about giving people space not only to read, but to reflect on what
a story might be teaching them.

With your permission, I would love to introduce you to Pastor Blake, a
member of our team who leads initiatives focused on women’s spiritual
growth and encouragement. He would be interested in exploring whether there
might be a meaningful way for SuperSummary and 365 [name] to
collaborate, such as:

   - Featuring relevant study resources and insights on our platform
   - Having a conversation about the role of literature in reflection,
   learning, and personal growth
   - Sharing thoughtful reading or discussion content that encourages women
   to engage more deeply with stories and the lessons they carry

I believe a conversation could open up some interesting possibilities,
particularly around using literature as a starting point for meaningful
reflection and encouragement.

Would you be open to a conversation with Pastor Blake about the possibility
of collaborating?

Thank you for the work you’re doing to make literature more approachable
and thought-provoking. I appreciate the idea that a good story can become
even more meaningful when we take the time to stop, ask questions, and
consider what it has to say to us.

Blessings,
[name]

Segmentation: SuperSummary – Making Complex Ideas Accessible to Every Reader
Feedback:
Dear SuperSummary Team,

I recently came across your Study Guide for [name] *Naked
Economics: Undressing the Dismal Science* and found myself genuinely
impressed by the depth and clarity of your analysis. I'm writing to express
my appreciation for a resource that transforms a potentially daunting
subject economics into something approachable, digestible, and genuinely
useful for readers of all backgrounds.

Your guide covers all 13 chapters with "clear, well-organized summaries and
expert analysis," offering not just surface-level synopses but "core
frameworks and concepts explained in plain language," key takeaways,
contextual analysis of the author's background and intent, and
discussion-ready questions for book clubs. What stays with me is your
mission: to help readers move "from reading to understanding to action." As
one reviewer put it, SuperSummary "really helps me understand all I read
and even helps me catch things I may have missed." Another book club leader
called your guides "a game-changer," saying they can now "enjoy reading the
club selections without taking copious notes."

What distinguishes SuperSummary is your commitment to quality and
accessibility. Since 2015, you've developed over 10,000 Study Guides
"crafted by literary scholars and subject-matter experts" to "support
learning, spark meaningful discussions, and inspire new discoveries." The
stats speak for themselves: 99% of book club members say your guides
improve their discussions, 91% say they deepen their understanding, and 94%
say they find everything they need in your guides. You serve everyone from
professionals sharpening their thinking to teachers engaging students, from
lifelong learners to avid readers seeking new layers of meaning. There's
something wonderful about a company that takes the "dismal science" and
makes it accessible, practical, and even enjoyable.

I also find your journey as a publisher deeply inspiring. You've built a
library of over 10,000 titles spanning "popular fiction, contemporary
literature, nonfiction favorites, and classroom classics." You've created a
trusted resource that readers, teachers, and book clubs have relied on for
nearly a decade. There's something remarkable about a team that has
dedicated itself to helping people *understand* what they read not just
consume it. Your Instagram presence (@supersummary) and your commitment to
"expert insights and in-depth analysis" suggest a team that genuinely cares
about education and engagement.

I'm writing because I would love to know more about three things:

1. The Selection Process. With over 10,000 Study Guides, how do you decide
which books to cover? What draws you to a particular work popular demand,
educational relevance, or something else?

2. The Craft of Summarizing. Your guides offer more than "just a
surface-level synopsis." How do your subject-matter experts and literary
scholars approach the challenge of distilling complex ideas into clear,
accessible summaries without losing nuance or depth?

3. The Reader Community. You serve everyone from book clubs to
professionals to students. How do you design your guides to be equally
valuable across such different audiences, and what have you learned from
your readers over the past decade?

I understand SuperSummary has been creating Study Guides since 2015. If you
are ever open to a conversation whether for a podcast, a feature article,
or simply an exchange of ideas I would be deeply honoured.

Thank you for the clarity, the insight, and the reminder that even the
"dismal science" can be undressed and made beautiful.

Warmly and respectfully,

[name]

Segmentation: Author Spotlight Invitation – Study Guide: The Birchbark House
Feedback:
Hello SuperSummary Team,

I hope you're doing well.

My name is Robyn, and I am an organizer of the NYC Philosophy and
Psychology Readers Community, a reading community of more than 8,000
members dedicated to thoughtful discussions of philosophy, psychology,
literature, and other intellectually engaging works.

I recently came across your *Study Guide: The Birchbark House by Louise
Erdrich* and was particularly interested in the way it supports readers in
moving beyond simply following the story toward a deeper examination of its
characters, themes, symbols, motifs, and underlying ideas. The guide's
chapter-by-chapter analysis and discussion-focused approach offer a
valuable framework for readers who want to engage more thoughtfully with
Erdrich's work, and we believe that perspective would resonate well with
our community.

What especially stood out to us is the guide's emphasis on encouraging
critical thinking and meaningful discussion. By bringing together literary
analysis, character development, thematic exploration, important
quotations, and discussion prompts, the guide creates useful opportunities
for readers to consider *The Birchbark House* from multiple perspectives
and engage more deeply with the questions the novel raises.

We would be delighted to feature *Study Guide: The Birchbark House* as part
of an upcoming Author Spotlight. For each spotlight, our members engage
with the featured work in advance before coming together for a dedicated
discussion. We would be honored to invite a representative from
SuperSummary to join us at the conclusion of the reading for a live
conversation and Q&A with our community.

One of the qualities that makes these conversations especially rewarding is
that participants are encouraged to prepare beforehand. This creates an
environment where questions are informed, discussions are substantive, and
the conversation can focus on the ideas, approaches, and perspectives that
make the featured work distinctive.

We see our Author Spotlight series as an opportunity to foster meaningful
dialogue between creators of intellectual and literary resources and
engaged readers. It is a chance to explore the thinking behind a work in
greater depth and create a thoughtful conversation that extends beyond the
reading itself.

If this invitation is of interest, I would be delighted to share additional
details about the event format, proposed timeline, and answer any questions
you may have.

Would you be open to having *Study Guide: The Birchbark House* featured in
an upcoming Author Spotlight with the NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers
Community?

Thank you for your time and consideration. We would be honored to have the
opportunity to introduce your work to our community and, if your schedule
permits, to welcome a representative from SuperSummary for a conversation
with our readers.

Warm regards,

Robyn

Organizer

NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community

Hey Support,

When we ask marketers how they are using AI, we’re seeing two distinct groups:

One group we’ll call the “Explorers.” They are stress testing AI tools, using them as presented and not tinkering too much with context or settings or workflows. This is a good place to start.

The other group we’ll call the “Optimizers.” They are redoing workflows and knowledge bases to be readable and usable by AI. This results in better outputs and unlocks totally new ways of working.

This is a newsletter about becoming the latter group.

In this issue, we explore how to set up a “living knowledge” system using internal interviews. Then we have a highlight reel of our latest couple of webinars about using your existing work to inform your AI workflows.

You’ve already done most of this work, now put it to use.

👇

Latest insights (see the archive https://autonomous.activecampaign.com/)

**You don’t have an AI problem. You have a “Dead Knowledge” problem**

**You'll learn…**

* Why your stalled AI project might have more to do with your “dead knowledge" than your tools or processes.

* How to capture “living knowledge” with interviews and NotebookLM. See what to upload, actual prompts, and exact tools to avoid AI slop.

* The evaluation prompt that turns the system into your first reviewer before doing anything internal (the same one that cut a major agency's proposal revisions from 30 to 3 and flagged ideas the client's CEO had already rejected).

Sending emails to your whole list feels efficient, right up until the unsubscribe rate skyrockets. This week, we’re showing you how Active Intelligence can do the sorting for you.

**Paste this into Active Intelligence:**

**Look at my email engagement from the last 60 days and create 3 audience segments for my next campaign: 1) Highly engaged (opened or clicked at least 3 emails), 2) At-risk (opened 1 to 2 emails, no clicks), 3) Inactive (no opens in 60+ days). Tell me how many contacts are in each segment and briefly describe how I should treat each group.**
